A french-speaking channel initially though out to share knowledge, help beginners overcome their apprehension to start coding which can be pretty daunting by fooling around and doing nonsensical projects, then it evolved to a bit of gaming and lots of chatting but the core values remain unchanged.

basics.summary:
Likes to dev smoothly and specially likes creating the necessary conditions to do so. Deeply convinced that communication is the cornerstone of our profession.
Fascinated by what the agile mindset, software craftship, devops and many more (lesser known or less obvious) approaches can bring to the table in terms of communication and natural incentive to take a step back.
Vocal advocate of de popularization AND democratization of the best practices of software craft (meaningful testing, (A)TDD, BDD, commentless, ...), devOps (build as code, semper virens trunk, containerization, ...), or agile (ardent promoter of giving teams the means to achieve true autonomy and maturity).

awards.title: Top 10 - Java category
awards.awarder: Meilleur Dev De France (a french coding contest)
awards.summary:
I ended 7th out of around 50 contestants.
It's kind of lame that that's the only trophy I have.
But I don't participate in that many contests anyways, and that was a ton of fun so ^^ I show it off as a sweet memory :)
awards.addendum:
Anyways my line of work is never as much "coding" as it's "developing".
My job's main issue have far less to do with solving tedious algorithmic problems or even to be on the bleeding edge of the capacities of any given language/tool/framework (and I'm the first saddened by that observation, every time I do, I have the time of my life) than it has to do with communicating, active listening and passing on understanding (which isn't any less fascinating).
But on the off chance that you're looking for someone to make them do code-katas and coding challenges all day : don't hesitate one second ! I'd be having a blast (and I have a feeling I could become very good pretty quick).
